original_question: Classify all recurrent one-sided sequences x in A^N and two-sided sequences x in A^Z whose maximal pattern complexity satisfies p*(n)=2n for every n >= 1. Equivalently, determine exactly which sequences are pattern Sturmian in the sense of Kamae and Zamboni.
target_in_paper: Section 2.1, Problem 2.1.1: "Determine all single sided (resp. double sided) sequences that are pattern Sturmian." The relevant notation and hypotheses are introduced immediately before it: A is a finite alphabet, x is a recurrent one-sided or two-sided sequence, p*(n) is the Kamae–Zamboni maximal pattern complexity, and "pattern Sturmian" means p*(n)=2n for every n≥1. The nearby Theorem 2.1.1 and Conjecture 2.1.1 motivate the problem but are not themselves the classification question. ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/id/eprint/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))
correct_elements: Your draft already captures the right open problem: it asks for a classification of pattern Sturmian sequences, includes both one-sided and two-sided sequences, keeps the recurrence hypothesis, and uses the defining equality p*(n)=2n for all n≥1. That is essentially the content of Problem 2.1.1 together with the preceding definition of pattern Sturmian. ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/id/eprint/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))

refined_question: Let A be a finite alphabet, and let x be a recurrent sequence (that is, every finite block occurring in x occurs infinitely often), either one-sided x∈A^N or two-sided x∈A^Z. For n≥1 define its maximal pattern complexity by p_x^*(n)=sup_{0=τ(0)<...<τ(n−1)} #{x_{m+τ(0)}x_{m+τ(1)}...x_{m+τ(n−1)} : m∈Z}, with the natural one-sided modification m∈N when x∈A^N. A sequence x is called pattern Sturmian if p_x^*(n)=2n for every n≥1. Determine all one-sided and two-sided sequences x that are pattern Sturmian. ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/id/eprint/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))
justification: The draft clearly targets the symbolic-dynamical classification problem in Section 2.1, not the spectral conjecture that follows it. Immediately before Problem 2.1.1, the paper fixes a finite alphabet A, assumes x is recurrent, defines the Kamae–Zamboni maximal pattern complexity p*(n), and defines pattern Sturmian by the condition p*(n)=2n for all n≥1. Problem 2.1.1 then asks to determine all single sided and double sided sequences with that property. Theorem 2.1.1 and Conjecture 2.1.1 explain why this classification matters for Schrödinger operators, but they are not the statement your draft is primarily capturing. ([eprints.whiterose.ac.uk](https://eprints.whiterose.ac.uk/id/eprint/109936/8/art3A1010072Fs40598_016_0046_6.pdf))
